acks.detail: Task 8 — fleet/exe-verbs.json: the seven allow-list attestations (`rename`/`new`/`ssh-key`/`tag` on the 2026-08-30 golden and orchestrator builds, `ls`/`stat` on the 2026-08-28 capacity reading, `billing` on the 2026-09-01 width read) — Each entry records a live operator sitting against a real exe.dev account. tests/test_runbook_exe_verbs.py verifies shape only (three non-empty fields, ISO `on` date, no overlap with the provision set — all pass, and the RUNBOOK's nine verbs are fully covered by provision's {cp, rm} plus these seven). Nothing in the tree can confirm the sittings happened. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

The exam pins that the sentence is rendered verbatim (it is, at fleet/RUNBOOK.md:197), but the numbers and the missing-package claim are only checkable by ssh'ing the orchestrator. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

Tasks 6 + 7 — the driver→sandbox plan-in-assignment handoff end to end — The two halves agree by construction and I verified the shared literal matches on both sides (fleet/provision.mjs:253 emits `plan: {text, verdicts}`; fleet/shim-main.mjs:938/:900 reads it and materialises `.claude/ultrapowers/assignment-<runId>/<basename>` plus the sibling `<stem>.gate-verdicts.json`, which compile_plan.py:530 resolves beside the plan). But no test drives a real drive into a real sandbox shim, so a full `--plan-from-assignment` run — the engine actually compiling from the materialised copy — has never executed. Each half is pinned only against its own stub. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

Task 5 — fleet/sweep-branches.mjs against a live origin and a live `gh` — Per the plan's own global constraint, every git/gh call in fleet/tests/test_sweep_branches.mjs travels through a canned `exec` seam (no network, no `gh`). The command strings the module builds are pinned byte-for-byte, but the verb has never been run against a real GitHub remote — in particular `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all --json state,number --limit 1`'s real output shape and `git push origin --delete`'s real behaviour are unexercised.
